confirm.stopDesc: The EBS volume is retained. You can start it again at any time.
confirm.deleteDesc: This cannot be undone. The EBS volume is deleted as well.

list.description: A Jupyter / Code Editor development environment based on SageMaker Spaces. Start and stop it at any time; the EBS volume is retained.
list.filterHint: Filtering is limited to the latest 5000 items.

tips.template: The application type the dev instance uses (jupyter-lab / code-editor). It inherits the default image and launch command from the template; resources are chosen through a resource template when you create it.
tips.spec: Resources requested by this dev instance: CPU cores · memory · GPUs · EBS storage. The EBS volume is retained when stopped and destroyed on deletion (not recoverable).
tips.status: The dev instance's own runtime status (CR phase). Available: running; Stopped: stopped; Provisioning: being created; Degraded: unhealthy; and so on. Click the magnifier for the full status details.
tips.queueStatus: The dev instance's status in the Kueue scheduling queue (separate from its own status). Queued: waiting for quota; Admitted: admitted by Kueue; Evicted: evicted; and so on.

statusTip.progressing: Pod creation / image pull / EBS mount / SSM agent start / Jupyter or Code Editor initialization. The most common "waiting to load" state.
statusTip.available: Target state: the Pod is Ready and the IDE port is up. Click "Connect" to open the IDE or get a shell over SSM. started_at is taken from this condition's lastTransitionTime.
statusTip.stopped: You clicked "Stop" (patch desiredStatus=Stopped) or the instance was reclaimed for being idle. The Pod is destroyed and its GPU/CPU released; the EBS volume is retained, and "Start" restores it.
statusTip.degraded: The Pod keeps crash-looping, the node is lost, the EBS mount failed, SSM registration timed out, and so on. Check the Conditions message in the "Status timeline (K8s Conditions)" card on the details page.

detail.title: Dev Instance Details
detail.ebsNote: EBS volume · retained when stopped, destroyed when deleted (not recoverable)

connect.title: Connect to dev instance
connect.notReady: The instance is not ready yet, so there is no connection info. Wait for phase=Running and the DNS record to sync (about 30-60s), then click Refresh.

ssh.title: Native SSH · fixed DNS name, unchanged after stop/start
ssh.desc: Connect to the dev instance directly over the VPC internal network (port 22222). You must configure your SSH public key first (① below). This internal domain name only resolves from machines in the same VPC as the cluster or with a connected network.

key.title: ① First-time setup · paste your SSH public key
key.desc: Generate a key pair on your local machine if you don't have one: ssh-keygen -t ed25519. Paste the full contents of your local ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub below and click "Write automatically"; the platform writes it to the dev instance's authorized_keys for you (the private key stays on your machine, never share it).
key.manualHint: The dev instance must be running. If automatic writing is unavailable, run this manually in the Code Editor terminal:
key.echoLine: echo "<paste the full contents of your local ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub>" >> ~/.ssh/authorized_keys && \
key.empty: Paste your local SSH public key first (the full line of the .pub file).
key.written: Public key written. You can now connect over SSH.
key.writeFailed: Failed to write the public key
key.copied: Copied the public key setup command

terminal.title: ② Terminal · open a shell on the dev instance
terminal.desc: After the public key is set up, copy the whole line below and run it in a macOS/Linux terminal to enter the dev instance ({{user}}).

vscode.title: ③ VSCode Remote-SSH · edit code graphically
vscode.desc: ① Install the Remote - SSH extension in VSCode ② Append the whole block below to ~/.ssh/config ③ Press ⌘⇧P → "Remote-SSH: Connect to Host" → pick the alias after Host on the first line.

connect.refreshHint: · The DNS name never changes. If the instance was just created or started, the connection info may only be available after DNS syncs; refresh to fetch it.

resize.title: Resize
resize.confirmContent: This restarts the current Pod and interrupts any running sessions (data in /home/sagemaker-user is kept; in-memory data is not). Are you sure you want to continue?
resize.loadMountsFailed: Failed to load the mount list
resize.runningWarning: Resizing recreates the Pod · the current session is interrupted; /home/sagemaker-user is kept, in-memory data is not
resize.poolTooltip: The resource pool cannot be changed. To switch between the CPU and GPU pools, recreate the dev instance.
resize.noTemplates: No resource templates yet · contact a Workspace admin to create one
resize.storageTooltip: Choose a subset of the FSx / S3 storage already attached to the Workspace · additions and removals take effect immediately (the new mounts are used after the Pod is recreated).
resize.storageNote: Storage capacity cannot be changed here (EBS volumes cannot be expanded). For a larger /home/sagemaker-user, recreate the dev instance.

create.title: New Dev Instance
create.storageTooltip: Choose a subset of the FSx / S3 storage already attached to the Workspace · none is selected by default; leave empty to skip.
create.envTooltip: Environment variables are injected into the container. Any row with a non-empty key is saved; leave empty to skip this step.

messages.loadMountsFailed: Failed to load the Workspace mount list
messages.cloneTemplateChanged: Clone: the resource template for the original configuration has changed or been deleted. Select a resource template again.
messages.cloneFetchFailed: Clone: failed to load the source dev instance configuration
messages.mountMissing: Mount {{path}} is not in the list (unexpected)

basic.namePattern: Must start with a lowercase letter, 3-63 characters; a-z, 0-9 and - are allowed.

image.label: Image (full name, including tag)
image.help: Choose from the images under "Asset Management → Image" whose purpose includes dev instance (dev), or type any full image URI (including the tag). Private ECR is only supported in the AWS account and Region this platform runs in; images from other accounts or Regions cannot be pulled.
image.empty: No images available for dev instances (dev). Register one under <registry>"Asset Management → Image"</registry> first, or type an image URI directly.
image.hint: The dropdown lists images under "Image" whose purpose includes dev instance (dev); you can also type any image URI.
image.required: Select or enter an image URI.

resource.poolTooltip: Choose a GPU or CPU resource pool. The dev instance is scheduled onto any instance type in that pool (a CPU pool may contain several types).
resource.templateTooltip: Resources (GPU/CPU/memory) are governed by templates maintained by admins and cannot be entered manually.
resource.templatePlaceholder: Select a resource template (maintained by admins)
resource.noTemplates: No resource templates yet · ask a Workspace admin to create one in Admin Console → Resource Template
resource.poolNoTypes: The current Workspace has no available instance types in the {{pool}} resource pool · contact a platform admin
resource.poolNoTypesValidator: The current Workspace has no available instance types in this resource pool.
resource.storageTooltip: Disk size of the dev instance home directory /home/sagemaker-user (a separate EBS volume). Conda environments, pip packages, code, and intermediate artifacts all live here, so leave plenty of room (deep learning environments take a lot of space). The volume is retained when the dev instance is stopped and the data is still there after a restart; deleting the dev instance destroys it as well, and it cannot be recovered. For large datasets or data that must be shared, mount FSx instead.
resource.perNodeSpecTooltip: GPU/CPU/memory are governed by the resource template and cannot be entered manually; switching templates syncs them automatically.
resource.memoryPolicy: Memory below 8 GiB is blocked by the official policy (required for Remote Access).
resource.quotaOver: · over quota; it will wait for quota after you submit
resource.quotaCollecting_one: · {{count}} GPU in total · remaining quota is being collected
resource.quotaCollecting_other: · {{count}} GPUs in total · remaining quota is being collected
